title: Menus
scenario: A 4,096-row MenuPopup with 100 keyboard steps and an open/close cycle; ten menu sessions in an embedded-only application. Proves G10, G3.

adapter.description: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (popup windows: the thread's shared native device stack, hardware first, WARP fallback)

cppAllocations: not counted: this executable does not replace the allocation functions
drawCalls: not counted: frame.drawCalls is 0 without the counting wrappers

phases.name: warm
phases.description: the application's first menu session: open the 4,096-row menu, then close it; first-use state settles

phases.name: open
phases.description: open the 4,096-row menu with its first row selected and pump until it has rendered

phases.name: keyboard
phases.description: one Down key to the open popup per step, then its render: a steady popup frame

phases.name: close
phases.description: Escape to the popup; pump until the session has ended and the popup is destroyed

phases.name: cycle
phases.description: the open/close cycle again: step 0 opens the 4,096-row menu, step 1 closes it

phases.name: sessions
phases.description: ten whole menu sessions of the embedded-only application, one per step: open a 12-row menu, render, Escape, destroyed

memory.trackedLiveBytes: not measured: this executable does not replace the allocation functions

G13.budget: idle native window <= 8 MB private above process entry at 1080p
G13.counter: private bytes after the last phase, shown, minus private bytes at process entry
local video memory usage of the process, hidden (a hidden embedded view is its minimized state)
G13.reason: software adapter: rendering uses system memory, which private bytes count

G13.counter: tracked live C++ bytes after the build divided by the controls of the built tree (host attachment included)
G13.reason: this executable does not replace the allocation functions

G13.budget: <= 1 KB per visible single-line Grid cell

timing.reason: timing comes only from performance-timing.ps1 on a hardware adapter in a quiet window (W0.2); counts and memory are recorded here
